---
name: Test naming convention
description: unit-tests-java8 tests are named DeclaringType_method (highest declaring type), always @Override+@Test, delegate to super; full rules live in the project skill unit-tests-java8-naming
type: feedback
---

The full rules are in the project skill `.claude/skills/unit-tests-java8-naming/SKILL.md`. Load it before touching any test in unit-tests-java8.

Core: the name is `DeclaringType_method[_chained]`, where the prefix is the type HIGHEST up the hierarchy that declares the method under test (not the class getting coverage, not a scenario). Overrides keep the same name, carry `@Override` + `@Test`, call `XTestCase.super.sameName()` when the parent's assertions apply, and add a commented section. No scenario-named methods and no helper methods.

**Why:** The user has corrected this repeatedly (scenario names, helpers like `assertSelfReferentialMakeStringAndAppendString`, missing super delegation in BiMapTestCase/MapIterableTestCase, OrderedHashMapTest having too many non-@Override tests). An earlier version of this memory wrongly said the prefix comes from where the test lives rather than the declaring type.

**How to apply:** Before writing a test, find the declaring type of the method under test and look for an existing test with that name to override.

Related: [[feedback_coverage_in_contract_superclasses]], [[project_ordered_hash_map_pr]]

---
name: test-against-real-blueprint-corpus
description: Before reporting blueprint parsing/panel work done, run it over the top-favorited factorioprints corpus in jsdom and in a real browser
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Before telling the user a change to parsing, mod detection, lint, or any blueprint panel is done, run it against real blueprints, in jsdom and in a real browser. The top ~1000 most-favorited factorioprints blueprints span Factorio 0.14 through 2.0 formats and many mods.

**Why:** On 2026-10-07 the user found crashes and false "Unknown names" just by pasting popular blueprints into the preview, and said "you aren't testing very much before taking my attention." On 2026-10-08 they asked for more browser testing than spot-checking three URLs. Corpus runs found crashes, false mod verdicts, a lint hang, and an out-of-memory failure that unit tests missed.

**How to apply:**
- `scripts/corpus/fetch-top-blueprints.sh <dir> [count]` downloads `<key>.txt` strings the way the app does: the key CDN first, then Firebase. The CDN sometimes serves an older version than Firebase, so don't build a corpus from Firebase alone.
- `CORPUS_DIR=<dir> node node_modules/vitest/dist/cli.js run --project unit test/corpus/corpus.test.tsx` renders every panel for every nested blueprint (about 2 minutes for 1000).
- Build (`vp run build`), serve with `npx wrangler pages dev dist --port 5174`, then `npx tsx scripts/corpus/browser-check.ts http://localhost:5174 <dir> 6` loads each blueprint and its largest child in Chromium. It fails on page errors, error alerts, lint failures and hangs, and reports the longest main-thread task.
- Node's own fetch fails on this machine with EBADF, so use curl. Playwright's Chromium works.
- Pre-0.15 `H4sI…` strings (gzipped Lua) are unsupported, so expect them to fail.
- `src/parsing/types.ts` only described 2.0 shapes. Widening a type to the real 0.x/1.1 shape and letting the compiler find consumers works well.
- `npx tsgo --noEmit` at the repo root checks nothing (the root tsconfig has `files: []`). Use `-p tsconfig.app.json` (and node/functions/scripts).

Related: [[preview-needs-secure-context]]

---
name: maze-design-decisions
description: What Craig has confirmed, rejected, and left open for the maze game's design, as of 2026-09-19
metadata:
  type: project
---

Craig's original spec: 3D maze, 2D minimap in a corner, walk it yourself or a Windows 95 screensaver-style autopilot, objects used to solve a puzzle to escape, crank looks around, D-pad moves, A picks up, B drops.

**Confirmed wanted by Craig on 2026-09-19** (after playing the first build, which he said runs at a great frame rate):

- Fog-of-war automap: the minimap reveals only visited cells. No chalk marks or breadcrumbs, since fog of war covers it.
- Ariadne's thread: hold B and crank backwards to reel back along your path.
- Crank the portcullis open after solving the puzzle.
- "Dock to dream": putting the crank away hands over to the autopilot.
- Landmarks to help orientation: pictures on walls, shapes on the floor or ceiling.
- An object that flips the world upside down (from the Windows 95 maze).
- Maze sizes as difficulty. Best times per size are NOT needed.
- A daily maze generated from a date seed.
- Head bob, and maybe sprite bob. A compass strip.
- Sound, including a proximity hum for shapes.
- Osmos-like ambient music whose pitch changes with proximity to the exit (in Osmos it follows speed).
- Housekeeping: launcher card and icon (definitely), save and resume a run.

**Rejected:** accelerometer lean or peek ("too gimmicky, don't add that"). Measuring device frame rate is unnecessary.

**Still Claude's unconfirmed defaults:** D-pad left/right sidesteps with the crank out and turns with it docked; three-shape pedestal puzzle; shapes hover at eye level; screensaver mode has no puzzle and rolls into a new maze at the exit.

**Why:** Craig says yes to many ideas at once and wants momentum, but wants each idea as its own commit from a task list.
**How to apply:** Work from `.llm/todo.md`, one task per commit, `just precommit` green before each. Do not re-propose the rejected ideas. See [[sibling-playdate-projects]] and [[one-commit-per-task]].

Present review-walk items through `AskUserQuestion`. Batching **up to 4 questions in one call is fine** — that is what the tool is for.

What is not fine:

**How to apply:** in the recurring/due walks, the inbox walk, refine-journal and meta-feedback, put every decision inside an `AskUserQuestion` call, up to 4 questions at a time. This does not conflict with [[feedback_daily_review_never_pause_for_scope]]: never ask *whether* to keep going, just keep asking until the set is done.

Related: [[feedback_actionable_content_in_ask_tool]] — each question still carries everything needed to decide inside the question body.

---
name: factorio-migration-renames
description: "Measured impact of FBSR migration-rename support: ~2,800 Factorio Prints blueprints affected, driven almost entirely by two inserter renames"
metadata:
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 7d131901-7c87-4a97-bc6a-6ae8dfc22fd9
  modified: 2026-08-19T15:30:00.000Z
---

Factorio ships prototype renames in `data/<mod>/migrations/*.json` and applies them when importing an old blueprint; FBSR did not, so renamed prototypes rendered as "?". Implemented on FBSR branch `blueprint-migrations` (cut from `upstream/master` for a clean PR to demod) and cherry-picked onto `factorio-school-production`.

**Measured 2026-08-19, replacing an earlier over-optimistic estimate.** Ground truth came from rendering each renamed name alone on a stock bot and a migration-enabled bot and comparing image bytes — a name's render changes if and only if migration fixed it. Of the **99 renamed entity+tile names, only 14 were actually broken before**; the other 85 already rendered, because those prototypes still exist in current data. On a fresh random sample of 398 blueprints (site has 17,931): **70.6% are pre-2.0**, and **15.8% contain a name migration now fixes, extrapolating to ~2,838 blueprints**. That number is carried almost entirely by `filter-inserter` (41 of 398) and `stack-filter-inserter` (39). "Affected" is not "fully fixed" — such a blueprint may still have unrenderable names from missing mods.

**The semantics that matter, learned from the real files.** Every vanilla section uses the list-of-pairs shape (mods may use the dict shape, so handle both). Each migration file must be applied as ONE simultaneous substitution, not rename-by-rename: base's `1.2.0 stack inserter rename.json` swaps `stack-inserter` and `bulk-inserter` with each other, so sequential application sends both to the same prototype. Files apply in order and an earlier file must never see a later file's output — `stack-filter-inserter` → `bulk-inserter` in 2.0.0 must not then be re-run through 1.2.0. Naive flatten-and-chase-the-chain gets all of these wrong.

Renames are applied **only as a fallback after a name fails to resolve**. That ordering is not merely conservative, it is what makes the feature correct without tracking blueprint versions: the 1.2.0 swap would otherwise rewrite a *current* blueprint's `bulk-inserter` into `stack-inserter`.

Renames are read from the install at profile build time and stored as `migrations.json` in the asset zip, so rendering still needs no Factorio install (see [[blueprint-bot-local-asset-builds]]). The entry is ~5 KB and depends only on the install, so **existing asset zips can be retrofitted with `zip vanilla.zip migrations.json` instead of a full rebuild**; zips without the entry keep working.

Testing FBSR locally on macOS fails — `webp-imageio` has no arm64 native, so `AtlasPackage.readAtlases` throws. Run the bot in Docker instead, with `-i` (it exits on stdin EOF), `-e JAVA_MAX_HEAP`, and only **one container at a time** (two 6 GB emulated JVMs get OOM-killed, exit 137).

---
name: fbe-fork-link-format
description: How to link the playground into the Factorio Blueprint Editor fork, via the factorioprints.xyz position API
metadata:
  type: reference
---

teoxoy/factorio-blueprint-editor is unmaintained. The live fork is
https://github.com/FactoryGameFan/factorio-blueprint-editor deployed at
https://fbe.factorygamefan.com/ (maintained by wormeyman, Cloudflare Workers
paid plan, so linking traffic there was agreed to on Discord Aug 2026).

Link format: `?source=<blueprint string or blueprint-hosting url>` plus optional
`&index=<n>`. Preferred source is the Factorio Prints API:

    https://factorioprints.xyz/api/blueprintData/<sha1>/position/<0-based path>

**Why:** FactoryGameFan/factorio-blueprint-editor#276 (merged 2026-08-27) makes
the editor pass an `/api/` path through untouched, so this addresses one
blueprint inside a book without putting the blueprint in the URL.

Verified against production:

- `factorioprints.xyz` is the same API as `www.factorio.school`, one corpus —
  factorio.school keys resolve there too.
- The sha is **SHA-1 of the raw blueprint string** (the API also reports it as
  `blueprintString.sha` on `/api/blueprint/<key>`).
- Positions are **0-based** dotted; the playground's `selection` is 1-based.
- `/api/blueprintData/<firebase key>` answers 410 — it wants a sha.

Also: the editor parses the param by hand — `p.split('=')[1]` then
`decodeURIComponent` — so a bare `=` (base64 padding) truncates a blueprint
string. Always `encodeURIComponent` the value.

**How to apply:** `src/lib/factorioBlueprintEditor.ts` — `buildApiSourceUrl`,
`toPositionPath`, `blueprintSha1`, and `buildEditorUrl`, which prefers the API
url, then the blueprint string, then the source url (Cloudflare rejects URLs
over 16 KB). The sha is computed in `blueprintFetcher` and only for hosts the
API holds. See [[playground-selection-url-format]].
